what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the person's posts in tools/social-posts, read from their own post records through the run's records door.

payload.label: Posting calendar
payload.job: Show what this person is posting between two times, and which drafts have no time yet, so a post can be given a time or moved to another
payload.description: Give from and to (dates and times with their zone). Returns posts: each post whose scheduled time falls in between (or, sent without a time, when it was sent), earliest first, with at, status, words and can_move; and unscheduled: the drafts and approved posts with no time yet. A post gets a new time through draft_post with post_id and scheduled_for, which makes an approved or scheduled post a draft again to approve. Its screen is the month and hour calendar, where a post is dragged to its time.

from.description: The start of the span, like 2026-10-01T00:00:00-04:00

to.description: The end of the span, after from

provenance.source: trillion media-workspace scheduled-calendar.mjs and calendar-placement.mjs (the Mac's Schedule month, week and day views), rebuilt on src/social-posts.mjs calendar, the same read list_post_calendar makes (a2fdfe6), ported to the records door

screen.label: Posting calendar
screen.about: When each of your posts goes out.

payload.label: How each post did
payload.job: Show how each of this person's published posts did in each place it went: that place's own counts, the visitors its link brought and what they bought
payload.description: Give observations (each place's own counts for a post, read with that place's tools: { post_id, account_id, metrics: { name: number }, observed_at } or { platform_post_id, account_id?, metrics }), visits and conversions (as tool:break-down-visits-and-sales takes them: { visitor, project?, signals: { utm_content, ... } } and { visitor, project?, value? }) and optionally post_ids. Reads the person's post records and returns posts: one row per place a post was published to that has a count, a visit or a conversion, with post_id, account_id, title, platform_post_id, url, metrics, observed_at, brought ({ visits, conversions, value }, only what was counted) and evidence. A visit counts for a place only when its utm_content is exactly that post's post_id (the post went to one place), the place's own post id, or post_id::account_id; a token that could name several places counts for none. Nothing missing is shown as zero.

post_ids.description: Only these posts (post_id values from tool:read-post-calendar)

observations.description: Each place's own counts for a post

visits.description: First-touch visits with their link signals

conversions.description: Sign-ups or sales by visitor, with value

provenance.source: bitfield-packages packages/content-analytics read-data/post-performance-attribution.ts (the join, unchanged but for its local types), read over the person's post records through the records door

payload.label: Where a post can go
payload.job: List the accounts this person can post to, each ready or not and why, and each place they have no account for yet
payload.description: Reads the person's connection records. Returns destinations: each account_id (the connection id), platform, label, name and ready, with said when it is not ready (a field the place needs that the connection lacks); not_connected: each place with no account yet; and said. Use the account_id values as tool:draft-a-post destinations. It changes nothing.

provenance.source: the posting owner of the person's posts (draft, check, approve, set for its time, take back), moved here with its ready check and place rows; read and written over the person's post and connection records through the records door

payload.label: Draft a post
payload.job: Keep a post as a draft for the person to look at: its words, its video or picture, where it goes and when
payload.description: Give caption (the words), media (the file as the person's files list it: { identity, name?, media_type?, byte_length? }) with media_facts ({ duration_seconds, width, height } the file does not say), destinations (account_id values from tool:list-post-destinations), caption_by_platform ({ platform: words }), settings_by_platform ({ platform: { ... } }, like a video title), link (an https page; it is added after the words, tagged with the post and the place), scheduled_for (a date and time with its zone), time_zone, source ({ kind, id } of the record it came from, kept as given), format_id, reaches (the people it contacts first, each with where they were found) and drafted_by (the AI writing it). Give post_id to change a draft; changing an approved post, or a scheduled one nothing was sent for, makes it a draft again. Returns post, ready (as tool:check-a-post gives it) and said. Nothing is posted.

post_id.description: A post_id from tool:draft-a-post or tool:read-post-calendar

provenance.source: the posting owner of the person's posts (draft, check, approve, set for its time, take back), moved here with its ready check and place rows; read and written over the person's post and connection records through the records door

input.caption: A sample draft that goes nowhere yet

payload.label: Check a post
payload.job: Say whether a post is ready for each place it is going, and what each place will refuse, before it is approved or set to go
payload.description: Give post_id. Returns, for each destination, ready, problems (what that place will refuse, in plain words: words too long, a video or picture it needs, a kind or size of file it does not take, a setting it needs such as a video title) and not_checked (what could not be compared here, such as a video's length nobody gave, or whether the file is still in the person's files); and for the post, ready and said. Fix a problem with tool:draft-a-post. It changes nothing.

post_id.description: A post_id from tool:draft-a-post or tool:read-post-calendar

payload.label: Approve a post
payload.job: Approve a drafted post exactly as it was reviewed, so it may be set to go
payload.description: Give post_id and expected_values (the complete approval_values of the post as it was reviewed); expected_values is required, and approval is refused when its words, file, destinations or time changed since. A post going nowhere yet is refused. approved_by names who approved it. Returns post and said.

post_id.description: A post_id from tool:draft-a-post or tool:read-post-calendar

payload.label: Publish a post now
payload.job: Queue an approved post for immediate sending through each destination's existing send row
payload.description: Give post_id and expected_values (the complete approval_values snapshot reviewed for this action). It is refused if the post changed, is not approved, or is not ready for every destination. When ready, it sets the post's time to now and queues the existing at-its-time wake; this action itself sends nothing and does not say the post was published. The wake and each destination's send row record the actual outcome. Repeating the same request while it is queued returns the existing state without arming another send. A destination whose outcome is not known is never sent again automatically. Returns post_id, status, post, ready and said.

post_id.description: A post_id from tool:draft-a-post or tool:read-post-calendar

expected_values.description: The complete approval_values from the post as reviewed

provenance.source: the posting owner of the person's posts, using the existing post wake and each place's send and delivery-record owner

payload.label: Set a post to go at its time
payload.job: Set an approved post to go out at its scheduled time, once it is ready for every place it is going; nothing is sent now
payload.description: Give post_id of an approved post whose scheduled_for is still ahead. It is checked for every destination (as tool:check-a-post does); when ready, its status becomes scheduled and it waits for its time, and when not, it stays approved and said gives what each place is missing. Nothing is sent by this tool. tool:take-back-a-post makes a scheduled post a draft again. Returns post_id, status, post, ready and said.

post_id.description: A post_id from tool:draft-a-post or tool:read-post-calendar

payload.label: Send a post to YouTube
payload.job: Send one of the person's approved posts to one of their YouTube accounts once its time has come, and keep where it went
payload.description: Give post_id (an approved or scheduled post whose time has come) and account_id (one of its destinations: a youtube connection, service_connection:youtube or service_connection:youtube:<account>). The engine hands this run only that account's held values; they reach www.googleapis.com, youtube.googleapis.com only, as each request leaves. The destination is marked not known before sending, so a cut-off send is never repeated by itself: give resend: true only after looking on YouTube. A destination that already has the post is not sent it again. A post with a file hands the place that file from the person's files: a share it streams (a signed link that expires) or the file's bytes streamed to it, never a copy kept here. Returns post_id, status, post (with each destination's status, url and error in plain words) and said. This posts publicly on the person's account: run it only with the person's yes for this post.

post_id.description: A post_id from tool:draft-a-post or tool:read-post-calendar

resend.description: Send again to a destination whose outcome is not known, after looking on the place

armed_at.description: Given by the post's own wake (tool:send-each-post-at-its-time) when it runs this at the post's time: the armed_at the post was set with. Nothing is sent once the post no longer carries it

payload.label: Send each post at its time
payload.job: When the person's posts change, set each post that is set to go at its time to be sent then, to each of its destinations, by that place's send row
payload.description: Runs on its own once the person switches on its wake (at-its-time): each time their posts change, it reads the changed posts, and for each one set to go at its time (tool:set-a-post-to-go-at-its-time) it sets one run of the place's send row (tool:send-a-post-to-<place>) per destination still to be sent, at the post's scheduled_for. That run sends only while the post is still set to go as it was then, so a post taken back, changed or set again sends nothing at the old time. It sends nothing itself, polls nothing and keeps nothing. Its rights are the ones the sends it sets need (the person's posts, their connections and their files), because each send reaches only what this wake was granted. Returns set (each post, destination, send row and time), left_out (each send not set, with why) and said.

provenance.source: the engine's wake primitive (a record wake answering timed runs, each paid from the firing's budget under its grant), used for the person's posts in place of a self-hosted scheduler or a repeat that polls

payload.label: Save a snippet
payload.job: Save words I send again and again as a snippet, with blanks like {name} to fill each time, or change one I saved
payload.description: Give title (what you call it) and text (the words, with {name} where something changes each time; a blank is a lowercase name in braces), and tags (short words) if you like. Without snippet_id it makes a new snippet; with snippet_id (from tool:find-snippets) it changes that one, keeping the fields left out. Give expected_set_at (the set_at tool:find-snippets showed) to refuse the change when it was saved again since. Returns snippet: snippet_id, title, text, tags, blanks, set_at, uses. Refuses a snippet with no title or no words, an unknown snippet_id, and a 501st snippet. A snippet is the person's own snippet record; saving sends nothing anywhere.

snippet_id.description: A snippet_id from tool:find-snippets, to change that snippet

title.description: What the snippet is called, at most 120 characters

text.description: Its words, like Thanks {name}, see you {day}.

tags.description: Short words to find it by

expected_set_at.description: The set_at last read; the change is refused when it was saved since

payload.label: Find snippets
payload.job: Find the snippets I saved, by a word in them or a tag, so I can put one into what I am writing
payload.description: Give query (every word must be in the title, words or tags) and tag, both optional, and limit (at most 100). Returns snippets, most recently used or saved first, each with snippet_id, title, text, tags, blanks (the {name} blanks in it), set_at, uses and used_at; and more, how many matched beyond limit. Changes nothing.

payload.label: Use a snippet
payload.job: Fill in one of my snippets with this time's names and give me its words to put in what I am writing
payload.description: Give snippet_id (from tool:find-snippets) and values: { name: words } for each {name} blank. Returns snippet_id, title, text (the words with every given blank filled wherever it appears), left_blank (the blanks given no value, left exactly as written) and said naming them, so nothing is sent with a hole unseen. It counts the use (uses, used_at) and never changes the snippet's words. It sends nothing. Refuses an unknown snippet_id.

values.description: The words for each blank, like { "name": "Ana" }

payload.label: Keep a conversation summary
payload.job: Keep a short summary of this conversation, so the next AI that opens it reads a few lines instead of every message
payload.description: Give conversation_id (and app), summary (at most 4000 characters) and latest: { id, at } of the conversation's newest message now, as the messages owner shows it (its newest message from reading the conversation). The summary covers through that message; keeping again replaces it. Returns summary (summary_id, app, conversation_id, summary, through_message_id, through_at, set_at) and said. Refuses a missing conversation_id, an empty summary, and a conversation with no latest message. The messages themselves are not touched; the words it says name trillion's read_messages and save_thread_summary tools.

conversation_id.description: The conversation's id, as the messages it is in show it

app.description: The app the conversation is in, like Email (optional)

summary.description: The summary, in a few lines

latest.description: The conversation's newest message now: its id and time

payload.description: Give conversation_id (and app) and message_times: the times of the conversation's newest messages as the messages owner shows them (its newest page, like the last 100, is enough). Returns summary (null when none is kept yet), newer_messages (how many of message_times come after the message the summary covers through), stale (newer_messages above 0) and said, so a stale summary is never taken for the conversation's present. payload.label: Check the YouTube connection
payload.job: Check that the person's YouTube connection still reaches its channel, before a post is set to go there or a read is made
payload.description: Asks YouTube which channel the person's youtube connection signs in as, with the value the person's vault holds for it (placed only as the request leaves, never shown). Returns the channel's id, title and its uploads playlist id. A refusal (an expired, revoked or under-scoped sign-in) means the person connects YouTube again. It posts nothing and changes nothing.

account_id.description: One of the person's accounts of this kind, service_connection:youtube or service_connection:youtube:<account>, from tool:list-post-destinations

payload.label: List my YouTube videos
payload.job: List the videos of the person's own YouTube channel, public, unlisted and private as the connection allows, with each video's title and privacy status
payload.description: Lists the videos of the channel the person's youtube connection signs in as, from the channel's uploads playlist (give the playlist_id that tool:check-the-youtube-connection returns), page by page. Each video comes back with its id, title, privacy status (public, unlisted or private) and publish time; unlisted and private videos come back when the sign-in has read access to the channel, and a refusal means it does not. It posts nothing and changes nothing.

account_id.description: One of the person's accounts of this kind, service_connection:youtube or service_connection:youtube:<account>

playlist_id.description: The channel's uploads playlist id, from tool:check-the-youtube-connection

page_token.description: The nextPageToken the list before gave, for the next page
